* [https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/release-notes.html#release-notes-2-25-4|https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/release-notes.html#release-notes-2-25-4|smart-link] 
* [https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/releases/tag/rel%2F2.25.4|https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/releases/tag/rel%2F2.25.4|smart-link]

*NOTE:* There are a number of CVEs in log4j components that WildFly Core and WildFly *do not use* that are resolved in the log4j release we are moving to via this issue. But, WildFly Core and WildFly *are not affected* by those CVEs, since we do not provide the affected components. We only provide the log4j-api artifact, which is not impacted by the CVEs.

All server provisioning steps in WF Core project are using offline provisioning.
This option is hardcoded in wildfly-maven-plugin and galleon-maven-plugin configurations.

WildFly allows to control this with {{Dgalleon.offline=false}} property (default = true)

This request is about bringing the similar parameterization to WF Core.

items.fromString: {{TimeoutUtil.adjust(int)}} operates on plain integers which loses precision when applying the timeout factor – e.g. when adjusting 1 “second” will be not adjusted. Add a new {{adjust(Duration)}} overload that operates at nanosecond granularity and deprecate the integer-based method.
items.toString:
{{TimeoutUtil.adjust(int)}} operates on plain integers which loses precision when applying the timeout factor; e.g. when adjusting 1 “minute” by factor of +10% it will be adjusted by +100%. 

Proposal is to add a new {{adjust(Duration)}} overload that operates at nanosecond granularity and deprecate the integer-based method.

Also, introduce a style where all timeout fields are Durations and converted upon usage.

items.fromString:
The revert parameter for the installer high level operation allows to revert the current server installation to a certain revision. The name of this parameter produces some ambiguity since it is unclear whether the operation will revert the installation to a certain revision or whether it will revert the installation by undoing the changes introduced by the revision.

Probably revert --revision should be revert --to-revision or something so it is clear it is not reverting a particular revision, it is rolling back to an older revision.

CVE-2026-3505 - Unbounded PGP AEAD chunk size leads to pre-auth resource exhaustion.

CVE-2026-5588 - PKIX draft CompositeVerifier accepts empty signature sequence as valid.

CVE-2026-5598 - Non-constant time comparisons risk private key leakage in FrodoKEM.

\standalone\log\gc.log"" was unexpected at this time.{noformat}

h2. log4j2

----

* [https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/release-notes.html#release-notes-2-25-3|https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/release-notes.html#release-notes-2-25-3]
* [https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/releases/tag/rel%2F2.25.3|https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/releases/tag/rel%2F2.25.3]
* [https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/compare/rel/2.23.1...rel/2.25.3|https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/compare/rel/2.23.1...rel/2.25.3]



* [https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/release-notes.html#release-notes-2-25-4|https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/release-notes.html#release-notes-2-25-4|smart-link] 
* [https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/releases/tag/rel%2F2.25.4|https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j2/releases/tag/rel%2F2.25.4|smart-link]

*NOTE:* There are a number of CVEs in log4j components that WildFly Core and WildFly *do not use* that are resolved in the log4j release we are moving to via this issue. But, WildFly Core and WildFly *are not affected* by those CVEs, since we do not provide the affected components. We only provide the log4j-api artifact, which is not impacted by the CVEs.

items.fromString:
EE 11 uses Authentication 3.1; EE 10 uses 3.0.

Core provides this because it is a dep of the org.wildfly.security.authentication module, which in turn is an exported dep of org.wildfly.security.elytron-private.

Ideally we'd just ship the EE 11 variant in core and downgrade in full WF's wildfly-ee-10 feature pack, but I don't know if there are any testing aspects within WildFly Core that would need special handling.

Ideally we'd just ship the EE 11 variant in core and downgrade in full WF's wildfly-ee-10 feature pack, but I don't know if there are any testing aspects within WildFly Core that would need special handling.

items.fromString:
EE 11 uses Interceptors 2.2; EE 10 uses 2.1.

Core provides this because it is a dep of JBoss Invocation, which is a dep of the org.jboss.as.server module. Core doesn't actually use the parts of JBoss Invocation that involve Jakarta Interceptors.

Most likely we'll just provide Interceptors 2.2 from core and downgrade in full WF's wildfly-ee-10 FP. JBoss Invocation's dep is the 2.2 variant.

The difference between the two is some new, defaulted, methods in the InvocationContext interface.
